  null,null,"What is DuckDB? An in-process analytical SQL database built for fast OLAP queries. Why choose it? It runs columnar analytics on local files with no server to manage. Who uses it?   null,null,"DuckDB is an embedded OLAP database that runs entirely within your application process without requiring any server. If SQLite is the go-to embedded database for OLTP (transactional workloads), DuckDB is its analytical counterpart — processing complex analytical queries on large datasets with remarkable speed.   Summarize",0,"DuckDB 2026: Embedded OLAP Database — Data Analytics Without a Server","https://anhtu.dev/duckdb-2026-embedded-olap-database-data-analytics-without-server-1130"
  null,null,"May 9, 2026         What Is DuckDB? DuckDB is an in-process analytical database, often described as “SQLite for analytics.” It runs embedded inside your application—no server, no daemon, no port to open—yet delivers columnar, vectorized query execution that rivals dedicated OLAP systems for many workloads.   Summarize",0,"DuckDB in 2026: Embedded Analytics That Punches Above Its Weight","https://blog.nepexgroup.com/databases/analytics/2026/05/09/duckdb-embedded-analytics-modern-applications.html"
  null,null,"What if you could run SQL directly on your Pandas DataFrames without setting up a full database server?   null,null,"DuckDB can read Parquet, Arrow, CSV, JSON, and its own native format without copying data into the database first. When you point DuckDB at a directory of Parquet files on S3, it pushes down predicates to minimize data scanned, parallelize reads across files, and execute the query over the data in place.   null,null,"Overview DuckDB is an in-process OLAP SQL database designed for analytical workloads, running directly in Python, R, or as a standalone CLI with no server required — ideal for local data analysis, notebook-based EDA, and embedded analytics.   null,null,"Feb 1, 2026         It reads files directly. You don't import data into DuckDB before querying it. You point it at a Parquet file, a folder of Parquet files, or a Delta table, and it queries them in place. No ETL step, no intermediate copy. It's columnar and vectorized. DuckDB processes data in column-oriented batches, which is exactly how Parquet stores data on disk.
